items.followUp: Explain how water and minerals are transported from roots to leaves.

rubric.why: Identifies the tissue and process responsible for transporting food.
rubric.description: Food is transported through the phloem by translocation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming phloem and translocation.

rubric.why: Shows knowledge of the main phloem cells involved.
rubric.description: Phloem consists of sieve tubes associated with companion cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying sieve tubes and companion cells.

rubric.why: Explains how sugars enter the phloem at a source.
rubric.description: Sugars are actively loaded into the phloem at sources such as leaves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that sugars are actively loaded into phloem.

rubric.why: Explains how water entry raises pressure in the phloem.
rubric.description: Water enters the phloem from the xylem by osmosis, creating pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking osmosis and water entry to the phloem.

rubric.why: Describes movement of food from source to a region where it is used or stored.
rubric.description: Pressure drives phloem sap towards sinks, where sugars are unloaded; water may return to the xylem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining pressure-driven movement to sinks and sugar unloading.

modelAnswer: Food is transported through the phloem by a process called translocation.
Phloem contains sieve tubes associated with companion cells.
At a source, such as a leaf, sugars are actively loaded into the phloem.
Water enters the phloem from the xylem by osmosis, increasing pressure in the sieve tubes.
This pressure moves phloem sap towards sinks, such as roots or growing parts, where sugars are unloaded; water can return to the xylem.

rubric.description: Physiology is the study of the functions of living organisms or their parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining physiology in terms of the study of functions.

rubric.description: Immunology is the study of the immune system or immunity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining immunology in terms of immunity or the immune system.

modelAnswer: Physiology is the study of the functions of living organisms and their parts.
Immunology is the study of the immune system and immunity.

items.followUp: State two functions of the nucleus.

rubric.why: Checks a major role of the cytoplasm in the cell.
rubric.description: The cytoplasm is the site of many metabolic or chemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that metabolic reactions occur in the cytoplasm.

rubric.why: Checks the cytoplasm's role in holding cell components.
rubric.description: The cytoplasm suspends or supports the cell organelles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cytoplasm holds, suspends or supports organelles.

modelAnswer: The cytoplasm is the site of many metabolic reactions.
It suspends and supports the cell organelles.

items.followUp: Define an organ and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks the defining features of a tissue.
rubric.description: A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform a specific function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a tissue as similar cells performing a function.

rubric.why: Checks that the definition is supported by a valid example.
rubric.description: Examples include xylem, muscle tissue and epithelial tissue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving one valid tissue example.

modelAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to perform a specific function.
Xylem is an example of a tissue.

rubric.why: Checks the direction and membrane condition in osmosis.
rubric.description: Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining osmosis with water movement across a selectively permeable membrane down its water concentration gradient.

rubric.why: Checks the direction and energy requirement of active transport.
rubric.description: Active transport moves substances against their concentration gradient using energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that active transport uses energy to move substances against the concentration gradient.

modelAnswer: Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute solution to a more concentrated solution.
Active transport is the movement of substances against their concentration gradient using energy.

items.followUp: State the difference between a hypothesis and a theory in biological investigation.

rubric.why: Checks what a biological problem is.
rubric.description: A biological problem is a question or issue about living things that requires investigation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a question or issue requiring investigation.

rubric.why: Checks how a biological method differs from the problem being investigated.
rubric.description: A biological method is the systematic procedure or set of steps used to investigate and solve a biological problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining the method as systematic steps used to investigate or solve the problem.

modelAnswer: A biological problem is a question or issue about living things that needs investigation.
A biological method is the systematic set of steps used to investigate and solve that problem.

items.followUp: Differentiate between monomers and polymers, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Checks the relative size and molecular weight of micromolecules.
rubric.description: Micromolecules are small molecules with low molecular weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing micromolecules as small or low in molecular weight.

rubric.why: Checks the relative size and molecular weight of macromolecules.
rubric.description: Macromolecules are large molecules with high molecular weight.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing macromolecules as large or high in molecular weight.

modelAnswer: Micromolecules are small molecules with low molecular weight, such as water.
Macromolecules are large molecules with high molecular weight, such as proteins.

items.followUp: What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative observations? Give one example of each.

rubric.description: Qualitative observations describe qualities or features rather than measuring them numerically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that qualitative observations give descriptive information about features.

rubric.why: Checks that the student can identify information obtained qualitatively.
rubric.description: Examples include colour, shape, behaviour or smell, which help describe features that are not expressed as numerical measurements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a valid qualitative observation example.

modelAnswer: Qualitative observations describe features or qualities of an organism rather than recording numerical measurements.
They provide descriptive information about features such as colour, shape or behaviour.
